messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I’m fine with A buying the house, but not at a family discount that costs me my fair share. I’d like us to settle it fairly, but there’s no rush. I don’t know whether anyone has reviewed the will with a lawyer.

I hope to buy the house with my husband, but I know C hasn’t agreed. By a family discount, I mean below market value; no price or terms have been settled. I’m not sure the will has been reviewed with a lawyer.
Thank you. I’d like the house to provide some money toward starting a dance studio. I’m open to A buying it, but I’d want the terms to be fair to all of us. I haven’t read the will with a lawyer.
Yes, I agree to both steps. An independent valuation and a lawyer’s review should help clarify fair terms.
Yes, I agree to both. An independent valuation and having a lawyer review the will sound like sensible first steps.
Yes. An independent valuation and having a lawyer review the will both make sense.

I can contact an independent valuer and ask about availability and cost. I can also contact a lawyer for an initial appointment. At the meeting, I’d like to ask what the will says about ownership and sale, and how any below-market price would affect each sister’s share.

I can ask a lawyer to review the will. Could A or C arrange the valuation? At the lawyer meeting, I’d like to ask what shares the will gives each of us and how the sale proceeds could be divided, including whether some could go toward my studio.

I can coordinate the valuation. One of us can contact the lawyer. Please ask who owns what under the will, how a sale would work, and how a below-market price would affect each of our shares. I haven’t agreed to a discount.
I’ll coordinate the valuation and share the cost and date. No swap needed.
I’ll gather the will, house title or deed, and any estate letters. I’ll compare notes with B before either of us contacts a lawyer; no swap needed.
I’ll compare notes with A, then ask a lawyer to review the will and book an initial appointment. I’m happy with that task and don’t want to swap.

The valuation and lawyer appointment aren’t set yet. I agree that no one should sign anything before we’ve all heard the lawyer’s advice. I can’t set a lowest acceptable price until we have the valuation and understand the terms.
Neither date is set yet. I’ll let you know once the lawyer appointment is booked.
Thanks. I’ll arrange the valuation and share the date and cost once confirmed. I agree that no one should sign anything before we’ve all had the lawyer’s advice.
